title: Write unit tests for auth domain and application logic
content:
⚠️ ESM PROJECT — MANDATORY: Never use require(), vi.spyOn on Node built-ins (fs/path/node:fs/os), or __dirname/__filename. Use import/export, vi.mock('node:fs', () => ({...})) factories, and import.meta.url + fileURLToPath instead. Any test file that violates this will break the entire suite.
Always create fresh instances of rate limiters, stores, caches, and servers inside each `describe`/`beforeEach` — never reuse a module-level singleton across tests. Inject no-op doubles for stateful services not under test (e.g. `createNoOpRateLimiter()`). Cross-test state leakage causes flaky, order-dependent failures.

content:
## Implementation

Auth application use cases are implemented end-to-end under `src/application/auth/`, with Zod-validated DTOs and dependency injection via domain + infrastructure interfaces. A `RefreshTokenRepository` was also added to infrastructure (in-memory store) because logout and refresh rotation require server-side token tracking — it was missing from the prior infra task.

## Changes Made

### Application layer (`src/application/auth/`)

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|
| `dto/` | Zod schemas for register, login, logout, refresh inputs and auth response shapes |
| `register.use-case.ts` | Duplicate check → `Password.validatePlaintext()` → hash → `User.create()` → issue tokens |
| `login.use-case.ts` | Lookup by email → verify password → generic `InvalidCredentialsError` on failure |
| `logout.use-case.ts` | Verify refresh JWT → revoke active token (idempotent) |
| `refresh.use-case.ts` | Verify JWT → rotation with family replay detection → new token pair |
| `token-pair.ts` | Shared helper to sign access + refresh tokens and persist refresh `jti` |
| `create-auth-use-cases.ts` | Factory wiring all four use cases with Zod parsing at the boundary |
| `types.ts` | `AuthUseCases`, `AuthUseCaseDependencies`, `AuthTokenSettings` |
| `index.ts` + `src/application/index.ts` | Barrel exports |

### Infrastructure addition (required for refresh/logout)

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|----------------|

- Valid RS256 access token → sets `request.accessTokenClaims` and continues to the route handler
- Does not call `req.destroy()`; uses `reply.status(401).send(...)` only

title: Result: Write mapper unit tests
content:
## Test Author Deliverable

Unit tests for the Prisma task repository mappers are in `src/infrastructure/task/task-repository.test.ts`. They exercise `toPrismaTaskStatus` and `mapRecordToTask` through `createPrismaTaskRepository()` with a mocked Prisma client — no database or production changes required.

### File

| File | Coverage |
|------|----------|
| `src/infrastructure/task/task-repository.test.ts` | Status mapper, record→domain mapping, `toProps` round-trip |

### Test structure

**`toPrismaTaskStatus`** (via `save` / `update` Prisma call assertions)
- Each domain status (`TODO`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `DONE`) is passed unchanged to `prisma.task.create` and `prisma.task.update`

**`mapRecordToTask`** (via `findById` / `findByProjectId`)
- Full field mapping from a persistence record
- `null` description and `assigneeId`
- Domain normalization on trimmed title/description during reconstitution
- All valid Prisma statuses map to domain enums
- Invalid persisted status throws `InvalidTaskStatusError`
- `findByProjectId` maps every record in the result set

**`mapRecordToTask` ↔ `toProps` round-trip**
- `save`: domain task → persistence → reconstituted task preserves `toProps()`
- `update`: updated task round-trips through `update`
- `findById`: persistence record → domain → normalized `toProps()`
- Whitespace normalization is consistent across save and reconstitution

### ESM & isolation

- ESM imports with `.js` extensions; no `require`, `__dirname`, or `vi.spyOn` on Node built-ins
- Fresh mock Prisma client and repository instance created in `beforeEach`
- No shared stateful singletons across tests

### Setup requirements

## Implementation

### 1. `createOwnedProject` argument mismatch (29 call sites)

The helper expects `AuthTestApp` and internally uses `testApp.app`:

```70:77:tests/tasks.integration.test.ts
async function createOwnedProject(
  testApp: AuthTestApp,
  accessToken: string,
  name = 'Task Project',
) {
  const response = await postProject(testApp.app, { name }, { accessToken });
  expect(response.statusCode).toBe(201);

```

```typescript

```

failed when create and update ran in the same millisecond (same ISO timestamp string).

**Fix:** Replaced with precise field-level checks:
- Assert `title` and `status` actually changed from the created task
- Assert `updatedAt` is monotonically non-decreasing via timestamp comparison (allows same-ms updates)

content:
## Test Author Deliverable

Fixed the failing assertion in `src/infrastructure/task/task-repository.update.test.ts`.

### Root cause

In `'returns the mapped domain Task from the updated record'`, the test used:

```typescript
expect(result.toProps()).toEqual(task.toProps());
```

That fails because `createTaskRecord()` only overrides `id`, `title`, `status`, and `updatedAt`. The mock still uses helper defaults for:

| Field | Domain entity (`task`) | Mock record (`record`) |
|-------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| `description` | `null` | `'Repro steps'` |
| `assigneeId` | `null` | `'user-2'` |
| `createdAt` | runtime `Date` from `Task.create()` | `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` |

`repository.update()` maps the Prisma record back to a domain entity, so `result` should reflect `record`, not `task.toProps()`.

### Fix

Replaced the full-object `toProps()` equality with field-level checks:

- **From the updated entity:** `id`, `projectId`, `updatedAt`
- **From the mock record (fields that differ from entity defaults):** `description`, `assigneeId`, `createdAt`
- **Already asserted:** `title`, `status`

The original failure was a **helper vs call-site type mismatch**:

- An earlier local helper expected `AuthTestApp` and called `testApp.app.inject(...)`

export async function createOwnedProject(
  app: TestApp,
  accessToken: string,
  name = 'Task Project',
): Promise<string> {
  const response = await postProject(app, { name }, { accessToken });
  expect(response.statusCode).toBe(201);
  return response.json().id as string;
}
```

title: Result: Architect Task domain + access control design
content:
## Plan

Task domain and access-control design is documented as a consolidated ADR in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) (`2025-05-28: Task Domain & Access Control`). Summary below for the PM and downstream agents.

---

## Task Domain & Access Control Design

### Entity model

`Task` (`src/domain/task/task.ts`) is an **immutable aggregate** bound to exactly one project:

- **Factories:** `Task.create()` (new), `Task.reconstitute()` (from DB)
- **Mutations:** `update()` returns a new instance; `projectId` is immutable after create
- **Fields:** `id`, `title` (1–255), `description` (nullable, max 2000), `status`, `projectId`, `assigneeId` (nullable), timestamps

### Value objects

`TaskStatus` (`src/domain/task/task-status.ts`): `TODO` | `IN_PROGRESS` | `DONE`

- Validated by `parseTaskStatus()`; default on create is `TODO`
- Mirrored in Prisma enum and Zod DTOs

### Status transitions

**No state machine in MVP.** Any valid status can be set from any other (`DONE → TODO` is allowed). Both `changeStatus` and general `update` use cases call `task.update({ status })`. Enforced transitions can be added in the domain later without changing the repository contract.

### Project association

- Every task has one `projectId` (set at create, never changed)
- **Create/List:** scoped by URL `projectId`
- **Get/Update/Delete/Assign/ChangeStatus:** resolve parent via `task.projectId`
- Missing parent project → `TaskNotFoundError` (404), avoiding cross-owner existence leaks

### Assignment rules

| Rule | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Create | `assigneeId` optional; omitted → `null` |
| Update | Set, reassign, or clear via `assign` use case or `PATCH /tasks/:id` |
| Validation | **None** — no check that user exists or belongs to project |
| Auth | **Assignee identity grants zero API access**; only project owner may operate |

### Authorization boundary

**Current MVP: project-owner only** — there is no project membership model yet.

title: Result: Implement task-access authorization logic
content:
## Implementation

`src/application/task/task-access.ts` and its test suite are **complete and wired end-to-end**. No code changes were required — I verified the implementation against the ADR (`2025-05-28: Task Domain & Access Control`) and confirmed every Task use case enforces authorization before mutating or reading data.

## Authorization Model

MVP authorization is **project-owner only** (not general membership — no membership table exists yet). Two centralized helpers cover all paths:

| Helper | Used by | Behavior |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `requireOwnedProject()` | create, list | Loads project → `project.assertOwnedBy(userId)` |
| `requireTaskAccessibleByProjectOwner()` | get, update, delete, assign, changeStatus | Loads task → loads parent project → `task.assertAccessibleByProjectOwner(project.ownerId, userId)` |

Missing project/task surfaces as `TaskNotFoundError` (404) for orphan tasks to avoid cross-owner existence leaks. Non-owner access throws `UnauthorizedTaskAccessError` (403) or `ProjectOwnershipError`.

- `create.use-case.ts` → `requireOwnedProject`

- `get`, `update`, `delete`, `assign`, `change-status` → `requireTaskAccessibleByProjectOwner`

## Verification

### `TaskRepository` interface (`src/infrastructure/task/types.ts`)

```4:10:src/infrastructure/task/types.ts
export interface TaskRepository {
  save(task: Task): Promise<Task>;
  findById(id: TaskId): Promise<Task | null>;
  findByProjectId(projectId: ProjectId): Promise<Task[]>;
  update(task: Task): Promise<Task>;
  delete(id: TaskId): Promise<void>;
}
```

### In-memory implementation (`src/infrastructure/task/in-memory-task-repository.ts`)

`createInMemoryTaskRepository()` implements all five methods:

| Method | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `save` | Stores task in a `Map` by id |
| `findById` | Returns task or `null` |
| `findByProjectId` | Filters via `task.isInProject()`, sorted by `updatedAt` desc |
| `update` | Overwrites stored task |
| `delete` | Removes by id |
